title: platform-c-suite-opportunity-brief-and-field-evidence-2026
author: Marta Rodriguez
body:
Executive summary:

This brief is designed for platform and infrastructure leaders (CTO, VP Eng, Head of Platform) and their economic stakeholders (CFO, Head of Procurement). It equips field teams with concise business value messages, technical evidence, pricing scenarios, and an FAQ focused on security and compliance that addresses typical enterprise gating items during pilot-to-production conversations. Use it as a one-page narrative for executive meetings plus a tactical playbook for sales engineers during discovery and pilot design.

1) TL;DR value hypotheses (one-liners)
- Predictable inference economics: reduce per-token cost by 30%–60% vs unmanaged GPU fleets through batching, caching, and model routing.
- Consistent latency SLOs across clouds and private deployments: 95th percentile latency targets of 120–300ms for common generative workloads.
- Operational confidence: unified tooling for observability, rollout control, and failure recovery that reduces MTTR and rollout risk.

2) Target audiences and objectives
- CTO / VP Engineering: want reliability, predictable latency, integration effort estimation, and path-to-scale.
- Head of Platform / Infra: need capacity planning details, autoscale model, and compatibility with existing IaC and cloud accounts.
- CISO / Security Leader: require KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and evidence for data residency.
- CFO / Procurement: want clear pricing scenarios, committed costs, and ROI math.

3) Positioning pillars (short)
- Production-first: benchmarks and SLOs we can commit to and measure in the console.
- Flexible deployment: same API and ops for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Cost controls: explicit levers (batching, quantization profiles, model routing) with observable unit economics.

4) Top field messages (elevator + 3 minute tech summary)
- Elevator (30s): "Redwood Inference gives you enterprise-grade LLM inference with predictable cost and latency across hosted and private deployments, plus the operational tooling to safely scale to production."
- 3-minute technical summary: 1) Runtime optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching, kernel selection), 2) Deployment abstraction (pin versions, rollouts, failovers), 3) Observability & cost breakdown (per-token, per-route).

5) Competitive brief (concise)
- Competitors covered: Large public LLM APIs, cloud-managed endpoints, self-hosted inference runtimes.
- How to frame differences: focus on predictable economics + unified operations.

Competitive one-liners to use in field conversations:
- Public LLM API: "Fastest to start, but opacity in cost drivers and limited private deployment options. Redwood provides the same simplicity with explicit controls and private topology support."
- Cloud-managed endpoints: "Good infrastructure, but often lacks inference-specific runtime optimizations and unified rollout tooling across environments."
- Self-hosted runtimes: "Lower nominal cost possible, but requires specialized ops, RKIs for long-tail reliability, and no single-pane observability — Redwood packages the runtime and ops experience."

6) Pitch deck outline (recommended 10 slides + speaker notes)
- Slide 1: Title + one-line value prop. Speaker note: anchor to customer's top pain (cost, latency, compliance).
- Slide 2: Where teams waste money today. Note: show token costs, idle GPU time, and SLO misses.
- Slide 3: Our approach (runtime + orchestration + ops). Diagram: request routing -> runtime cluster -> observability.
- Slide 4: Deployment models and when to use them (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). Speaker note: recommend Private for regulated PII workloads.
- Slide 5: Measurable outcomes from pilots (latency, per-token cost, error reduction). Use anonymized metrics.
- Slide 6: Pricing & pilot offer (short term commitment scenarios).
- Slide 7: Security & compliance highlights (KMS, VPC, audit logs).
- Slide 8: Integration plan & timeline (2–8 weeks depending on scope).
- Slide 9: Customer references & case studies (short bullets).
- Slide 10: Next steps & asks (technical workshop, PO for pilot, contact info).

7) Pricing guidance (field playbook)
- Default pilot: 8-week engagement, hosted credits + onboarding support. Typical pilot scope: one model, two routes (low-latency and batch), up to 500k inference tokens/day.
- Pilot pricing (example scenarios, indicative):
  * Small pilot (proof): $15k flat for 8 weeks (includes 50k hosted tokens, 10 hours eng support, onboarding).
  * Platform pilot (integrator): $45k flat for 8 weeks (200k tokens, 30 hours eng support, SSO and VPC setup assistance).
  * Dedicated evaluation (capacity test): $120k 3-month evaluation (reserved nodes with throughput targets, includes performance tuning).
- Long-term pricing guidance: usage-based + optional reserved capacity. Example unit economics (for discussion only): $0.0006 / token-equivalent for hosted generation under optimized batching; dedicated pool models vary by instance type and amortized infra cost. Always attach a worked example for customer's expected annual tokens.

8) Pilot activation checklist (steps for field + SEs)
1) Discovery workshop (owners: AE + SE): collect scale targets, data residency, model selection, latency targets.
2) Security & contract check: run standard security questionnaire, verify legal T&Cs and data processing addendum.
3) Technical workshop: network connectivity (if Private), API keys, model mapping.
4) Instrumentation plan: define evaluation prompts, SLOs, and observability dashboard template.
5) Run pilot with weekly checkpoints and one optimization pass (quantization, batching).
6) Final report: performance, cost, recommended production architecture, and a one-page ROI.

9) Security & compliance FAQ (concise answers for prospect calls)
Q: How do you protect customer keys and secrets?
A: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted API, keys are tenant-isolated and stored encrypted at rest with per-tenant access controls.

Q: Can we keep data in our VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes. Private deployment supports a customer-controlled control plane and on-prem runtime options. We also support VPC peering and private link options for Dedicated.

Q: Do you provide audit logs for inference requests?
A: Yes. Audit logs are available as structured events (request id, model, route, timestamp, tokens, outcome) and can be exported to the customer's SIEM (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk). Retention policy is configurable per contract.

Q: How is sensitive data handled in model cache and KV stores?
A: Sensitive inputs are excluded from long-term cache by default. We provide configurable cache filters and optional encryption-at-rest for KV caches. For regulated workloads the recommended pattern is to use Private deployment with customer-managed storage.

Q: What compliance programs do you support?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is in process for ISO 27001 and GDPR-ready controls. We provide artifact bundles for SOC 2 and template DPIAs to accelerate customer reviews.

Q: How do you ensure availability and graceful degradation?
A: Smart routing and fallback policies allow automatic failover to compatible model variants or regions. SLA-backed Dedicated customers get defined uptime and latency targets; all customers benefit from canary rollouts and automatic circuit-breaking.

10) Two short anonymized case studies (one paragraph each)
- Global SaaS provider (Customer A) – challenge: unpredictable inference cost and high 95th percentile latency for chat. Outcome: after a 6-week pilot they achieved a 42% reduction in per-conversation inference cost and a 28% improvement in 95th percentile latency by enabling prefix caching and a small model routing policy.
- Financial data vendor (Customer B) – challenge: strict residency and audit requirements. Outcome: deployed Private control plane in a customer VPC with HSM KMS and reached sign-off for a compliance audit within 10 weeks; production rollout reduced MTTR by standardizing rollout policies and observability dashboards.

11) Conversation scripts (field-ready soundbites)
- For the CTO: "We treat inference like any other high-throughput service — we provide not just the runtime but the operational controls and metrics needed to make predictable investment decisions."
- For the CISO: "We can operate inside your trust boundary, integrate your KMS, and provide full audit evidence mapped to our controls."
- For the CFO: "We model your expected annual token usage and show you the conservative, mid, and aggressive savings scenarios; pilots include clear acceptance criteria so you can quantify ROI."

12) Assets & links for SEs (what to attach to the intro email)
- One-page ROI calculator (attach spreadsheet).
- 10-slide pitch deck (editable).
- Security artifact bundle (SOC 2 summary, network diagrams, KMS integration guide).
- Pilot statement of work template and onboarding checklist.

13) Owner, escalation, and feedback loop
- Document owner: Marta Rodriguez (go-to-market).
- Escalation: route urgent security questions to Priya Sethi (Security Engineering). For product/feature-related technical gaps, loop in Liam Chen (Product).
- Feedback: after each pilot the AE must submit a 1-page post-pilot summary to the sales-enablement mailbox and link the lessons in the related_pages list above.

Appendix: sample acceptance criteria (to include in pilot SOW)
- Latency: 95th percentile at or below agreed target for chosen route for at least 7 of 8 pilot weeks.
- Cost: per-unit cost under agreed threshold after tuning and the single optimization pass.
- Security: required network connectivity and KMS integration validated; necessary audit logs exported and verified.
- Business: defined success metrics (e.g., increased automation throughput, reduction in human review cost) with baseline and target values.

End of brief.
